The signed expansion into l and Δ is an identity. Its lower bound is obtained directly from the minimum effective denominator times the midpoint bit, and therefore retains the midpoint selector on the denominator term. Replacing the midpoint submeasure by the physical source measure minus its uncovered part is valid as an identity.

The inward part uses the common outward normal of the actual tight parallel faces. In the compatible midpoint setting this is the source face normal at both endpoint faces: a strict endpoint support excess would contradict midpoint support equality by combining it with a point of the other face. A common translation preserves the exact midpoint relation. At a coincident pure-base cap it leaves the closed bit unchanged, and at a continuous-normal coincidence it picks the inside or outside side. Proper in-face boundaries are null for the absolutely continuous marginals. Source d4b2499d695ba5c9 §6 (15)–(19) uses these same conventions.
